topic: Two siblings inherit their grandmother's house
text: Well, now, I hear the village elder was talking of young Eli and Miriam down by the creek. Seems their grandmother's house, the one at the edge of the woods, now belongs to them. It's a sturdy place, near the orchard where the apples grow fat and ripe by midsummer. I recall times when I'd help their grandmother with the hay, her fields always a bit wild, but good, with the rich soil she had. Those two never spent much time there, but I reckon it's a blessing. They'll have their hands full, what with the repairs and the memories. A house like that, it holds more than just walls and beams. It's been a while since the last of the old bloodline walked those halls. It's strange to think of them in that space now, setting down roots in a garden tended by another’s hands.
